annotation.authors_or_issuer: جناحي، و. ي. (University of Bahrain, College of Law)
key_provisions_or_claims: Surveys four doctrinal views of robots: person, thing, animal-like, or sui generis entity.
Robots may be treated as mechanical things under Article 175 of the Bahraini Civil Code, making the guardian liable.
Compulsory insurance for robot users covering all damage.
Regulate manufacture, use and operation of robots before market circulation.
Add a paragraph to Article 175 making the maker and programmer jointly liable, with a rebuttable presumption of fault, plus a black-box mechanism.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Lecture slides by a University of Bahrain law professor on civil liability for robot errors. They review robots' legal status (person, thing, animal-like, sui generis) and liability bases. They recommend compulsory insurance, pre-market regulation, and an amendment to Bahrain Civil Code Article 175 making makers and programmers liable.

annotation.title_en: Civil Liability for Errors Resulting from the Actions of Robots
